newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kurita sees higher earnings after planned merger.
newsitem.headline: Kurita sees higher earnings after planned merger.

text.p: Kurita Water Industries Ltd said on Monday that it planned to merge its machine maintenance unit into the parent company and that profits should rise after the move.
Kurita Technical Service, a wholly owned unit which maintains and repairs machines sold by Kurita, will be absorbed by the parent company on October 1, Kurita said in a statement.
The merger is aimed at strengthening the basis of Kurita's business and boosting its efficiency, Kurita said.
Kurita expects its parent current profit in the year to March 31, 1998, to be 21.10 billion yen and net profit to be 11.30 billion yen on sales of 150 billion yen.
It forecasts a 1998/99 parent current profit of 23.70 billion yen and a net profit of 12.45 billion yen on sales of 182 billion yen.
Kurita has forecast a parent current profit of 19.35 billion yen and net profit of 10.35 billion yen on sales of 137 billion yen in 1996/97, the last business year before the merger.
Kurita expects to pay a 14 yen annual dividend each in 1996/97, 1997/98 and 1998/99.
